I agree with the Router's severity ratings but elevate the concern due to the Pose Auditor's high-risk flag.
alignment_reasoning: The image is clearly a Spoonbill (Fine Grained Classifier Top-1). It matches the core diagnostic features: spatulate bill, long neck, wading posture. The deviation in leg color (pink vs generic black/grey) and bill color (pale vs yellow-tipped) are species-specific traits of the Roseate Spoonbill, not generation errors. Therefore, alignment is high despite strict checkpoint failures. The S-curve neck and body proportions are accurate.
artifact_reasoning: Significant structural uncertainty detected by the Pose Auditor (High Risk, 53% low-confidence keypoints). Visual inspection confirms subtle melting/smudging at the bill-face junction and inconsistent leg thickness/definition (left leg weaker than right). Feather textures on the neck show AI-style smoothing/painterly artifacts (Severity 2). While the overall shape is coherent, the lack of crisp anatomical definition in key areas (face, joints) prevents a higher artifact score. The image is better than the 'low' reference but worse than the 'high' reference due to these structural/textural softness issues.
